package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 through 2020.2.1 HF 1 (approximate, based on public reporting)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion software supply chain was compromised, resulting in the distribution of a backdoored update (Sunburst) to thousands of customers. The malicious code enabled remote access and control by attackers, facilitating widespread espionage and data exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup and during runtime, the code checks for network connectivity, beacons to a hardcoded command-and-control domain (avsvmcloud.com), and, if a command is received, executes attacker-supplied instructions, enabling remote control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces unauthorized network communications to an external domain and enables remote command execution, which is not expected in legitimate Orion updates.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Orion updates should not contain code that beacons to external C2 domains or executes remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may check for updates or telemetry, but not with obfuscated C2 logic or remote command execution.
key_indicators: Persistence within a core business logic DLL

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At service startup, the code checks for signs of analysis (e.g., running in a SolarWinds corporate domain, presence of debuggers, or virtual machines) and terminates if detected, evading detection by security researchers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-analysis and anti-debugging logic is a hallmark of malware attempting to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business logic should not terminate based on environment or analysis checks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or licensing checks may use environment detection, but not to evade security analysis.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into the SolarWinds Orion build pipeline and distributed via software update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of backdoored software to customer environments

attack_chain.action: Upon service startup, the malicious DLL performs anti-analysis checks to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of C2 beaconing logic if not in analysis environment

attack_chain.action: Malicious code beacons to external C2 domain and awaits attacker instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command execution and potential data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion services to avsvmcloud.com or similar C2 domains
Presence of obfuscated or non-standard logic in core Orion DLLs
Anti-analysis checks (domain, debugger, VM) in business logic assemblies
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected hash or size
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in Orion installation directory
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Beaconing patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion servers to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Perform file integrity checks on core Orion DLLs to detect unauthorized modifications. Analyze business logic assemblies for anti-analysis or obfuscated code. Correlate with threat intelligence on known Sunburst indicators.
